title: Research Without User Access
intro: When NDAs, procurement and security clearance block interviews and testing, there is still evidence available.

learn.title: Blocked, but not blind
learn.text:
**Often blocked:** recruiting end users, usability testing (IP and NDA), support logs and tickets, analytics (no data yet).

**Still possible:** task analysis and requirements, shadowing people doing similar tasks, interviewing customer success and domain experts, and reading job postings to map roles and tasks.

“Light the problem from many sources and you get a glimpse of the truth.”

try.q: What can job postings tell a researcher with no user access?
options: What the buying process looks like
try.explain: They map the work even when you can't observe it.

learn.title: The buyer is rarely the user
learn.text:
In enterprise there are **two experiences to design**: the customer organisation that buys, and the employees who use it.

Their criteria differ. The buyer weighs procurement, security and price; the user weighs whether they can get through the day.

Designing only for the buyer is how enterprise software earns its reputation.

try.q: Why does the buyer–user split matter for research?
options: They judge the product by different criteria
try.explain: Two audiences, two experiences to design.

learn.title: Start with trust
learn.text:
Enterprise stakeholders are protective of data, IP and internal politics.

**Small, low-risk first steps build the trust** that later opens access to real users.

Other routes meanwhile: map workflows into a service blueprint, use search trends and public forums to find frequent problems, and build an internal test lab with the colleagues closest to customers.

try.q: How do you eventually get access to real users in a protective organisation?
options: Build trust with small, low-risk steps
Add a research clause to the contract

test.q: Who can substitute for end users when access is blocked?
test.explain: Along with shadowing people doing similar tasks.

test.q: What should workflows be mapped into?
test.explain: It documents how the work actually runs.

test.q: What is an internal test lab, in this note?
options: Colleagues closest to customers, used as testers
A panel of recruited external users

test.q: Why use search trends and public forums?
test.explain: Public evidence when private evidence is blocked.

test.q: What is the metaphor for combining weak sources?
options: Lighting the problem from many sides
test.explain: No single source is sufficient; together they give a glimpse of the truth.
